From 1581dafaf0d34bc9c428a794a22110d7046d186d Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Nicolas Pitre <nico@fluxnic.net>
Date: Thu, 29 Feb 2024 17:15:27 -0500
Subject: [PATCH] vt: fix unicode buffer corruption when deleting characters

This is the same issue that was fixed for the VGA text buffer in commit
39cdb68c64d8 ("vt: fix memory overlapping when deleting chars in the
buffer"). The cure is also the same i.e. replace memcpy() with memmove()
due to the overlaping buffers.

Signed-off-by: Nicolas Pitre <nico@fluxnic.net>
Fixes: 81732c3b2fed ("tty vt: Fix line garbage in virtual console on command line edition")
Cc: stable <stable@kernel.org>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/sn184on2-3p0q-0qrq-0218-895349s4753o@syhkavp.arg
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

diff --git a/drivers/tty/vt/vt.c b/drivers/tty/vt/vt.c
index 156efda7c80d..38a765eadbe2 100644
--- a/drivers/tty/vt/vt.c
+++ b/drivers/tty/vt/vt.c
@@ -381,7 +381,7 @@ static void vc_uniscr_delete(struct vc_data *vc, unsigned int nr)
 		u32 *ln = vc->vc_uni_lines[vc->state.y];
 		unsigned int x = vc->state.x, cols = vc->vc_cols;
 
-		memcpy(&ln[x], &ln[x + nr], (cols - x - nr) * sizeof(*ln));
+		memmove(&ln[x], &ln[x + nr], (cols - x - nr) * sizeof(*ln));
 		memset32(&ln[cols - nr], ' ', nr);
 	}
 }
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/tty/vt/vt.c`**
- The function `vc_uniscr_delete` was modified to replace the `memcpy()` function with `memmove()`. This change was made in the line that handles the deletion of characters from the Unicode buffer, specifically when moving data within the same buffer where overlapping might occur.

### Relationships
- The modification addresses a bug related to buffer corruption when deleting characters, which is similar to a previously fixed issue in the VGA text buffer. The patch references a prior commit (39cdb68c64d8) that implemented the same solution (using `memmove()` instead of `memcpy()`) for a different buffer type. This indicates a consistent approach to resolving overlapping memory issues across different components of the virtual terminal (vt) subsystem. The patch also includes a "Fixes" tag that links it to another commit that introduced the problem, establishing a direct relationship between the bug and its resolution.

Here is the commit message:
vt: fix unicode buffer corruption when deleting characters

This is the same issue that was fixed for the VGA text buffer in commit
39cdb68c64d8 ("vt: fix memory overlapping when deleting chars in the
buffer"). The cure is also the same i.e. replace memcpy() with memmove()
due to the overlaping buffers.

Signed-off-by: Nicolas Pitre <nico@fluxnic.net>
Fixes: 81732c3b2fed ("tty vt: Fix line garbage in virtual console on command line edition")
Cc: stable <stable@kernel.org>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/sn184on2-3p0q-0qrq-0218-895349s4753o@syhkavp.arg
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

Here is the root cause:
The bug is caused by using `memcpy()` to move data within the same buffer when deleting characters, which can lead to memory corruption due to overlapping memory regions. This results in incorrect data being read or written, causing line garbage in the virtual console during command line editing.

Here is the patch:
 
 static void vc_uniscr_delete(struct vc_data *vc, unsigned int nr)
 {
 	if (vc->vc_uni_lines) {
 		u32 *ln = vc->vc_uni_lines[vc->state.y];
 		unsigned int x = vc->state.x, cols = vc->vc_cols;
 
-		memcpy(&ln[x], &ln[x + nr], (cols - x - nr) * sizeof(*ln));
+		memmove(&ln[x], &ln[x + nr], (cols - x - nr) * sizeof(*ln));
 		memset32(&ln[cols - nr], ' ', nr);
 	}
 }

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
memcpy(&ln[x], &ln[x + nr], (cols - x - nr) * sizeof(*ln));
```
Reason:
The use of `memcpy()` does not handle overlapping memory regions correctly. When the source and destination buffers overlap, `memcpy()` can lead to memory corruption, resulting in incorrect data being read or written. This is particularly problematic when deleting characters, as it can cause line garbage in the virtual console.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
memmove(&ln[x], &ln[x + nr], (cols - x - nr) * sizeof(*ln));
```
Reason:
Replacing `memcpy()` with `memmove()` allows for safe handling of overlapping memory regions. `memmove()` correctly manages the memory overlap by ensuring that the data is moved in a way that prevents corruption, thus resolving the issue of line garbage during command line editing in the virtual console.
